author: Hultzsch
asr_identification: Sarnath N of Benares; the edict pillar = Xuanzang's 70-ft pillar before Asoka's stupa in the Deer Park
evidence: Oertel's broken polished pillar with Asoka's edict and the lion capital with wheel; height c. 37 ft above ground (Oertel) vs Xuanzang's 70 ft
quote: The Chinese traveller, Hiuen Tsiang, saw on the site of the Migadaya a stone pillar which stood in front of a Stapa built by A&Okaraja, and which was about 70 feet high…Hiuen Tsiang seems to have overestimated its height, unless he refers to a different pillar
note: Agrees with Mizutani (Sarnath; pillar with the Dharmarajika stupa 07.01.03) and the notes. The edict itself does not name the place; the identification rests on the find-spot and Xuanzang.

author: Hultzsch
asr_identification: Rummindei pillar, Nepal Tarai = Lumbini; Xuanzang's 'river of oil' = Tilar-nadi
evidence: Asoka's inscription: the king visited 'because the Buddha Sakyamuni was born here' and exempted the village of Lummini from taxes; shaft split, horse capital lost (Mukherji); nativity sculpture in the temple
quote: Both Lummini and the modern name Rummindéi must be identical with the Lumbini grove, the traditional site of the Buddha's birth…which is now called Tilar-nadi
note: Inscription naming the place found in situ. Agrees with Mizutani and the notes (Rummindei; Oil River = Tilar Nadi).

author: Hultzsch
name_in_asr: stupa of the Buddha Konakamana (Nigali Sagar pillar)
asr_identification: Nigali Sagar pillar = the pillar Xuanzang saw before Kanakamuni's relic stupa; pillar not in situ, stupa not traced near it
evidence: Asoka's inscription: he enlarged the stupa of Konakamana to double its size and later erected the pillar; two broken pieces, c. 14 ft 9 in and 10 ft
quote: Hiuen Tsiang seems to mention the Nigali Sagar pillar…referred to by Hiuen Tsiang canhot be traced near the spot where the two portions of the pillar have been found
note: Agrees with Mizutani (Nigali Sagar pillar, disputed); since the pillar is not in situ the stupa site stays open, as in the notes (Araura-kot if displaced).

author: Hultzsch
asr_identification: Kosambi a provincial seat; Takshasila = Shahdheri, Rawalpindi district (Cunningham); Dhauli and Jaugada (Puri, Ganjam) in Asoka's Kalinga, Jaugada's district seat called Samapa
evidence: Kosambi edict addressed to the mahamatras at Kosambi; separate edicts at Dhauli and Jaugada
quote: Greeks, was identified by Cunningham with Shahdhéri in the Ravalpindi district, Panjab…To this province we have to allot Dhauli and Jaugada in the Puri and Ganjam districts
note: Taxila agrees with Mizutani. Jaugada (Mizutani's capital of Kongoda, 10.10) was Samapa under Asoka; says nothing about the 7th century.

author: Hultzsch
note: Footnote on Faxian's Na-pi-ka (Krakucchanda's birthplace) and the Brahmapurana's Nabhikapura; Faxian-only, no location.

author: Hultzsch
note: I-tsing's image of Asoka as a monk; Asoka's visit to the Samgha. No place.

author: Hultzsch
note: Footnote: Xuanzang's yojana as a day's march. No place.

author: Hultzsch
name_in_asr: Kosambi (Kosambi edict on the Allahabad-Kosam pillar)
asr_identification: Kosam
evidence: Edict to the mahamatras at Kosambi engraved on the pillar now at Allahabad
quote: This ancient city (Kausambi in Sanskrit) corresponds to the modern Kdsam
note: Agrees with Mizutani and the notes (Kosam).

author: Konow
note: Trogus/Strabo on the Saraucae and Asiani; Saka history. No Xiyu ji place located.

author: Konow

quote: to the country of T‘o-li, themodern Darel on the right bank of the Indus, opposite Chilas
note: Faxian's 陀歴 = Xuanzang's 達麗羅川; agrees with Mizutani (Darel). Konow only cites Stein.

author: Konow

note: Etymologies of Yue-chi. No place.

author: Konow
asr_identification: Tirath village on the border of Swat Kohistan = the footprint stone; Apalala's spring near the head of the Swat at Kalam (Deane)
evidence: Boulder with two large footprints and an 11-letter Kharoshthi inscription of c. the mid-1st c. BC, found by Sir Harold Deane; Xuanzang's distance 30 li SW of the spring, 250 li NE of Manglaur
quote: Near the village a rock or boulder, showing two large fadukas and below them a Kharoshthi is inscription of eleven letters. We are able to identify these footprints with absolute certainty…He locates it on the north bank of the Swat river thirty li to the south-west of the spring of the Naga Apalala
note: Agrees with Mizutani (Tirat) and the notes; supports the notes' head-of-Swat-at-Kalam for 03.01.03. An inscribed footprint stone at the spot Xuanzang describes.

author: Konow
note: Continuation of P17: palaeography of the Tirath inscription.

author: Konow
name_in_asr: rock where the Buddha dried his clothes
asr_identification: a rock in the upper Swat valley (provenance vague) whose estampage Stein took for the clothes-drying rock
evidence: Estampage showing a rock surface cut by natural cross-lines and traces of Kharoshthi, from one of Deane's (unreliable) agents
quote: Sir Aurel thinks that the impression has been taken on the rock where the Buddha was stated to have dried his clothes
note: Mizutani's 03.01.04a is the rock Stein later found by the road; here only an estampage of unknown provenance. No change.

author: Konow
name_in_asr: Takhasila (Taxila copper plate of Patika); Chukhsa
asr_identification: Taxila; Chukhsa = the Chach plain, Attock tahsil, near Taxila (Stein)
evidence: Patika copper plate (year 78) found at Taxila records a relic and a monastery at Kshema 'in the town of Takshasila, to the north'
quote: In the town of TakshaSila, to the north, the eastern region, Kshema by name…identified Qhukhsa with the present Chach or Chachh
note: An inscription found at Taxila that names Takshasila. Agrees with Mizutani and the notes.

author: Konow
asr_identification: Sirkap the chief settlement of Taxila in the Saka period; Kshema to its NE, unidentified
quote: The locality called Kshema cannot be identified…we must look for it to the north-east of that place
note: About the Saka city (Sirkap). Xuanzang's capital is Sirsukh (Mizutani after Marshall), so no conflict. Bühler (P104) took the plate's Takhasila for Sirsukh.

author: Konow
note: Mathura lion capital; the Guhavihara 'is not mentioned by the Chinese pilgrims'. No Xiyu ji place.

author: Konow
note: Mathura lion capital: Kusulua Patika = Patika of the Taxila plate. No location.

author: Konow
name_in_asr: Vajrastupa (Mount Banj inscription of the year 102)
asr_identification: Mount Banj (Mahaban spur, Buner) = site of the Bodhisattva's body-offering to the tigress (Stein); the inscribed Vajrastupa perhaps either of the two stupas
evidence: Kharoshthi inscription from Mount Banj naming a Vajra-stupa; Xuanzang's red soil and the 200-ft Asoka stupa to the N quoted
quote: Sir Aurel Stein has shown that the Mount Banj remains represent the site where the Chinese pilgrims located the incident in the career of the Bodhisattva, when he gave up his body to feed a hungry tigress…Either of these may have been the Yaj rastupa
note: Agrees with Mizutani (disputed) and the notes (Mount Banj). The inscription shows a stupa at the site but does not name the jataka.

author: Konow
note: Kurram/Taxila inscription grammar (Takshasilae tanuvaa). No location.

author: Konow

author: Konow
note: Sirkap silver vase: Chukhsa (Chachh) as a Saka province with Taxila its capital. Saka period; no Xiyu ji place located.

author: Konow
asr_identification: Taxila: vase from mound 13 W of Shahpur near the Chir Tope; ladles from Mahal close to Sirkap
evidence: Vase inscription 'this stupa was established ... in Takshasila'; ladles naming Takshasila from Marshall's excavations 1920-27
quote: By Sihila and Siharakshita, the brothers, this stupa was established in honour of all Buddhas, in TakshaSila…They were found during Sir John Marshall’s excavations in 1920-1, 1923-4, and 1926-7 at Mahal, close to Sirkap
note: The name Takshasila is attested on objects found at the site. Agrees with Mizutani and the notes.

author: Konow
asr_identification: Bedadi on the Siran river, c. 12 miles NNW of Mansehra, Hazara
evidence: Copper ladle bought c. 1920 from a villager who found it at Bedadi; gift to the Kasyapiya teachers 'in the Urasa kingdom'; Stein: old site with Azes, Kushan and Hindu Shahi coins
quote: Gift of Samgharakshita to the congregation of the four quarters, in the UraSa kingdom, of the Kafiyapiya teachers
note: An inscription naming Urasa found in Hazara. Confirms Urasa = Hazara (Mizutani, notes). The find-spot near Mansehra does not decide the capital (Haripur, Watters; Mangali, notes).

author: Konow
note: Jaulia inscription: personal name Rahula. False match.

author: Konow
note: Minor Sirkap cup inscriptions. No location.

author: Konow
asr_identification: Hashtnagar, eight villages on the left bank of the Swat above its confluence with the Kabul river (Prang, Charsadda, Rajar etc.) = Pushkalavati
evidence: Hashtnagar pedestal inscription; Marshall and Vogel's 1903 excavation of the Palatu Dheri mound near Rajar
quote: on the site of the ancient town Pushkalavatl, the Peukelaotis of Greek writers
note: Agrees with Mizutani (Charsadda) and the notes (Charsadda/Prang).

author: Konow
note: Reading of an inscription; Naugram find-spot. No Xiyu ji place.

author: Konow
note: Yakubi sculpture said to show the miracle of Sravasti. Iconography only.

author: Konow
asr_identification: Shah-ji-ki-Dheri mounds outside the Ganj gate of Peshawar = the great Kanishka stupa of the pilgrims
evidence: Spooner's 1908-09 excavation: remains of a large stupa, relic chamber, Kanishka casket with Kharoshthi inscriptions
quote: where Cunningham and Foucher had located the big Kanishka stiipa mentioned by Chinese pilgrims. This location has been proved to be correct through Dr. Spooner’s excavations in the years 1908 and 1909
note: Agrees with Mizutani and the notes.

author: Konow
note: Manikiala inscription grammar. No location.

author: Konow
asr_identification: Hidda, c. 5 miles S of Jalalabad = site of the pilgrims' ushnisha stupa
evidence: Masson's jar with an ink Kharoshthi inscription from one of the Hidda stupas
quote: The small village of Hidda is situated on a line of conglomerate elevations, about five miles to the south of Jalalabad. It was there that the Chinese pilgrims found the stupa said to contain the Lord’s ushniska
note: Agrees with Mizutani (Hadda).

author: Konow
note: Index. No content.

author: Bhandarkar (rev. Chhabra & Gai)
note: I-tsing's Sri-Gupta. No Xiyu ji place.

author: Bhandarkar (rev. Chhabra & Gai)
asr_identification: Takka kingdom between the Chenab and the Ravi in Xuanzang's time (Stein)
quote: In the time of Hiuen Tsiang, the Takka kingdom was well-known and was situated somewhere between the Chenab and Ravi
note: Narrower than Mizutani (Beas to Indus); fits the notes' central Punjab. Footnote only.

author: Bhandarkar (rev. Chhabra & Gai)
asr_identification: Dakshina Kosala = most of Raipur and Bilaspur districts, with Sambalpur and Sonpur
quote: it comprises the greater portions of the modern districts of Raipur and Bilaspur in Madhya Pradesh
note: Agrees with Mizutani's 'recent view' (upper Mahanadi). Allahabad pillar context.

author: Bhandarkar (rev. Chhabra & Gai)
asr_identification: Sripura = Sirpur, capital of Kosala c. AD 800 (Tivaradeva's charters), possibly earlier
evidence: Two charters of Tivaradeva, 'Supreme Lord of Kosala', issued from Sripura
quote: about the eighth century a.d. it was certainly Sripura, modern Sirpur, because it was from this place that Tivaradeva…Possibly Sripura was the capital of Kosala even in the time of the Ikshvakus
note: Inscriptional support for the notes' capital Sirpur, though c. 150 years after Xuanzang.

author: Bhandarkar (rev. Chhabra & Gai)
asr_identification: Samatata = E Mymensingh and Dacca E of the Brahmaputra, Sylhet, Tippera, Noakhali, capital Badkamta 12 miles W of Comilla (Bhattasali); Kamarupa = W Assam and N Bengal
evidence: Allahabad pillar names Samatata, Davaka, Kamarupa, Nepala, Kartripura as frontier states; Bhattasali used the Baghaura image inscription
quote: On the strength of these data and also the Baghaura image inscription, N. K. Bhattasali has satisfactorily identified it with the natural geographical unit…He further holds the opinion that Badkamta, twelve miles west of modern Comilla was the capital of Samatata
note: Agrees with Mizutani (Bad-Kamta) and the notes. Kamarupa as W Assam agrees.

author: Bhandarkar (rev. Chhabra & Gai)
asr_identification: Sialkot
quote: Its capital was l§akala which has been identified with Sialkot
note: Agrees with Mizutani and the notes. Passing remark.

author: Bhandarkar (rev. Chhabra & Gai)
note: Kakas, Sanakanikas round Bhilsa. Not Xiyu ji.

author: Bhandarkar (rev. Chhabra & Gai)
asr_identification: extensive mound on the N side of the Bodhi tree
quote: From tliis it appears that the monastery was built outside the northern gate of the wall of the Bodhi Tree…The site is now marked by an extensive mound on the
note: Agrees with Mizutani (mound N of the Mahabodhi temple) and the notes.

author: Bhandarkar (rev. Chhabra & Gai)
asr_identification: Kosam, c. 28 miles W by S of Allahabad
evidence: Allahabad pillar originally stood at Kausambi (Asoka's Kosambi edict on it)
quote: From one of these it is also quite clear that originally this pillar was standing at Kausambi, identified with Kosam, about 28 miles west by south from Allahabad
note: Agrees with Mizutani and the notes.

author: Bhandarkar (rev. Chhabra & Gai)
note: Saketa (Ayodhya) as the W limit of Chandragupta I; Pushkarana. No location of a Xiyu ji place.

author: Bhandarkar (rev. Chhabra & Gai)
note: Valhikas and Vishnupada of the Meharauli inscription. Not Xiyu ji.

author: Bhandarkar (rev. Chhabra & Gai)
asr_identification: Basarh, Muzaffarpur district
evidence: Bloch's excavation at Basarh: clay seal of Dhruvasvamini
quote: One seal of this queen (No. 13) was exhumed by the late Bloch during his excavations at Basarh in the Muzaffarpur District, Bihar, which has been identified with the ancient Vaisali
note: Agrees with Mizutani and the notes. See P71 for the seals that name Vaisali.

author: Bhandarkar (rev. Chhabra & Gai)
asr_identification: Xuanzang's Malava lay SE of the Mahi river and is distinct from Ujjayini
quote: It is forgotten, however, that this Malava was situated on the south-eastern side of the Mo-ko
note: Argues for the Gujarat (Mahi) view against Malava = Ujjain. Mizutani and the notes leave it undecided.

author: Bhandarkar (rev. Chhabra & Gai)
asr_identification: Basarh
evidence: Seals found at Basarh: Vaisali as seat of the Yuvaraja and HQ of Tirabhukti
quote: as is clear from the seals found at Basarh which is the modern representative of that place
note: Repeats P56.

author: Bhandarkar (rev. Chhabra & Gai)
asr_identification: Basarh (Basadh)
evidence: Seals of Govindagupta and Ghatotkachagupta found at Basarh
quote: That was the reason why the seal of Govindagupta (= Kumaragupta) was discovered at Basadh (=Vaisali)
note: Repeats P56.

asr_identification: Pundravardhana = Mahasthan, Bogra; Kotivarsha = Bangarh, Dinajpur; Basarh = Vaisali
evidence: Damodarpur plates of the Kotivarsha vishaya in the Pundravardhana bhukti; Bloch's adhikarana seals at Basarh
quote: Pundravardhana has now been identified with Mahasthan…in the Bogra District and Kotivarsha with Bangarh in the Dinajpur District
note: Agrees with Mizutani and the notes (capital Mahasthan). See P72.

asr_identification: Pushpapura/Kusumapura = Pataliputra = Patna, originally at the old Son confluence (now near Dinapore); Xuanzang's other Kusumapura = old name of Kanauj
evidence: Allahabad pillar verse 7 names Pushpa as Samudragupta's capital
quote: The antiquity of the name Kusumapura, is vouched for by Hiuen Tsiang…He tells us that the old capital of Kanyakubja, or Kanauj, was originally called Kusumapura
note: Agrees with Mizutani and the notes (Patna).

author: Bhandarkar (rev. Chhabra & Gai)
note: Aryavarta and Madhyadesa; Xuanzang cited in a footnote. No location.

asr_identification: Basarh
evidence: Bloch's seals at Basarh show Vaisali as HQ of the Vaisali vishaya and Tira-bhukti
quote: As Basarh has been correctly identified with Vaisali…from other seals found on this site it appears that Vaisali was the head-quarters
note: Seals naming Vaisali found at Basarh give inscriptional proof. Agrees with Mizutani and the notes.

author: Bhandarkar (rev. Chhabra & Gai)
asr_identification: Mahasthan, Bogra = Pundravardhana; Bhasu Bihar 4 miles W = Xuanzang's Po-shi-p'o monastery (Cunningham)
evidence: Mauryan Mahasthan fragment, picked up in the ruins, naming a royal granary at Pundranagara; Karatoya-mahatmya lists Mahasthan's holy spots as Pundra-kshetra
quote: In his account of Bhasu Bihar, four miles to the west of Mahasthan, he remarks that the Buddhist remains at this place corresponded both in description and position with those noted by Yuan Chwang…And as this fragmentary inscription was picked up from the ruins of Mahasthan, it is obvious that they represent the vestiges of the old Pundravardhana
note: An inscription naming the city found in its ruins. Agrees with Mizutani and the notes for 10.04 and 10.04.02.

author: Bhandarkar (rev. Chhabra & Gai)
note: Kotivarsha = Bangarh (Devikota). Not a Xiyu ji place.

name_in_asr: Urjayat, Raivataka, Girinagara, Surashtra (Junagadh rock inscription of Skandagupta)

note: Agrees with Mizutani (Ujjanta = Girnar; capital Junagadh) and the notes.

evidence: Prasasti (c. AD 600) of princess Isvara, of the Singhapura royal line, widow of a prince of Jalandhara; 12 kings listed
quote: the district over which her ancestors ruled layin the saine province…pura rdjya of our inscrfption may be safely identified with the kingdom of Sang-ho

asr_identification: Vadnagar (Vriddhanagara), Kheralu subdivision, Kadi district

author: Führer
asr_identification: Pabhosa hill c. 3 miles NW of Kosam = Xuanzang's stone dwelling of the venomous Naga (Buddha's shadow) by Kausambi; Adhichhatra = Ramnagar
evidence: Rock-cut cave with 2nd/1st-c. BC inscriptions of Ashadhasena of Adhichhatra; Jaina inscription of 1824 at Pabhosa naming Kausambi and Prabhasa; local tradition of a Naga in the cave
quote: Hiuen Tsiang’s statement that the cave is 8 or 9 lé to the south-west of Kausambf, is erroneous, as the hill bears north-west from the fort of Kosim
